Subject: Order form security exhibit — pen test window + SOC2 evidence

Hi Mina / Laura,

Uploading our initial redlines to the Order Form security exhibit for the upcoming procurement cycle. High-level asks from our side: 1) clarify pen-test notice and staging window, 2) explicit SOC 2 artifact cadence and where evidence will be shared, 3) language around data residency for evidence exports.

Key proposed redlines attached (MediVex_Redlines_v1.docx). Summary:
- Pen-test notice: 30-calendar-days prior written notice; 2-week staging window (we'll request ephemeral tenant access).
- Scope: tests limited to non-production subnets; require test plan and point(s) of contact.
- Evidence cadence: Quarterly SOC 2 snapshot (PDF + evidence index), plus ad-hoc evidence for major infra changes or incidents; preferred delivery to a secure GDrive folder we control.
- Data residency: any exported logs or PII must be anonymized or hosted in US regions only.

We're trying to keep this simple for legal, but we need operational clarity so our security team can schedule the exercise and procurement can complete the order form. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support ephemeral staging access and a secure evidence share as described?

Also copying our InfoSec mailbox so they can flag any technical constraints.

Thanks,
Elaine Brooks

Mina / Elaine — following up with a concrete redline suggestion based on operations and legal constraints. Tracked changes are attached (tracked_redline_orderform.docx). Short summary below so procurement has a single paragraph to show stakeholders:

Proposed Order Form language (summary):
- Penetration testing: Customer must provide at least 45 calendar days' written notice for full-scope penetration testing targeting production workloads; for tests targeting clearly labeled non-production environments, a 30 calendar day notice is acceptable. Tests must be limited to the agreed scope and must not attempt privilege escalation beyond test accounts provided. Customer to submit a test plan and list of IPs/domains to be exercised at least 5 business days before the test window.
- Staging access: Redwood will provide ephemeral staging credentials scoped to a test tenant; access will be revoked at the end of the agreed window. Redwood reserves the right to require an on-call ops contact during the test.
- Evidence & SOC 2 artifacts: Redwood will provide a quarterly SOC 2 snapshot consisting of: control descriptions, the latest SOC 2 report PDF, sample control test artifacts (anonymized), and an evidence index mapping artifacts to SOC 2 criteria. For ad-hoc evidence requests tied to a material infrastructure change or incident, Redwood will respond within 10 business days. Evidence delivery to a mutually agreed secure folder (customer-owned GDrive or SFTP).
- Data handling: Any customer-supplied production data used for testing must be limited and anonymized; Redwood will not permit tests that exfiltrate or export raw PII/PHI outside of approved regions.

Notes: the 45-day/30-day split gives us operational breathing room while still being responsive. The test plan / IP list requirement is key to avoiding accidental cross-tenant impact. If MediVex wants a 30-day standard for production, we will need an SLA exception and additional change freeze windows.

Please see the attached tracked_redline_orderform.docx for exact clause text. If this looks good I can push the tracked doc back to DocuSign for formal sign-off.

-Karthik

Karthik / Mina — thanks for the clear options and the tracked changes. We reviewed with InfoSec and procurement; here's our counter-proposal to converge quickly:

- Notice: MediVex accepts the 45-day requirement for full production tests, but requests that for pre-authorized non-production environments the notice be 30 days. We can add a 72-hour emergency access carveout for remediation-driven tests (documented and mutually approved).
- SOC 2 snapshot: Quarterly snapshots as suggested are fine. Please include the evidence index in machine-readable CSV form where possible — that will speed internal review.
- Data: We will only use non-production data for pen tests and can agree to anonymization language; however, we request explicit order-form language that any exported logs that could contain PHI must be redacted prior to transfer.

If Redwood can accept tracked language with the 45/30 split plus the 72-hour emergency carveout, MediVex is prepared to accept the DocuSign package and move to signature. I can route the DocuSign link to procurement once you confirm.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — copying procurement so they have visibility.

Thanks,
Elaine Brooks
Senior Counsel, MediVex Health
